questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to invest safely in Bitcoin and make a profit
What cryptocurrencies are and how Libra is different
How banks protect our money from criminals online
The history of the Swiss franc and its strength
questions.why: Sam explains cryptocurrencies and they discuss Facebook's plans for Libra.

questions.q: What is special about a cryptocurrency, according to Sam?
options: It is only digital and no bank or government controls it
It is printed and managed by a country's central bank
It can only be used in the one country that created it
It is made of special metal coins that are hard to copy
questions.why: He says it's purely digital and not controlled by banks or governments.

options: It will buy a large amount of Bitcoin
It will ban cryptocurrencies from its site
It is launching its own digital currency
It is opening a bank in Switzerland
questions.why: Catherine says Facebook announced they're launching their own digital currency, Libra.

questions.q: Why does Jemima Kelly say Libra isn't really a cryptocurrency?
options: It isn't digital
It is controlled by one government
It is only used on Facebook
It is backed by a group of real currencies
questions.why: It is backed up by a basket of currencies like the dollar, pound, euro and Swiss franc.

questions.q: Which currency is NOT mentioned as backing Libra?
options: The dollar
The euro
The Japanese yen
The Swiss franc
questions.why: She lists the dollar, the pound, the euro and the Swiss franc.

questions.q: What risk do ordinary cryptocurrencies have?
options: Their value can rise or fall a lot very quickly
They are easy to steal
They lose value slowly over time
They can't be exchanged for real money
questions.why: Sam says crypto markets are notoriously volatile, going up or down quickly.

questions.q: Why are most normal currencies more stable?
options: Far more people around the world use them
Governments and banks control them
They are made of metal and paper
They are older and have a longer history
questions.why: Sam says governments and banks control currencies to prevent big changes.

questions.q: Why does Sam compare cryptocurrencies to a self-driving car?
options: They are the future of transport
They are easy to use
They are controlled by computers that never fail
You can't control where they go, and it could end badly
questions.why: He says it might be an exciting ride, but it could end in disaster.
